note: Keyword retrieval, policy math, confidence threshold. Published first; scored 71% self-solve on its own 28 cases. Here it's rescored on the 52-case dev set that adds the first round of probe questions.
verdict: Baseline. Probing found typos, negation, refund-status and routing failures.

note: Fixed the probe failures: stemming and typo tolerance, negation, a refund-status rule, always honoring a request for a person, and separate safety, trust and specialist queues.
verdict: Overfit: perfect on dev, 25% safety recall and 2 wrong answers on unseen questions.

note: Fixed failure classes found on holdout 1, not individual questions: a safety vocabulary by category (medical, environment, personal safety, property crime), synonyms for rescheduling, guests, entry, pests and statements. Holdout 1 folded into dev; scored on a fresh holdout 2.
verdict: Not shippable: safety hand-off recall is 75% on unseen questions. Keyword retrieval is precise (no wrong answers) but misses paraphrases. Next: semantic retrieval behind the same harness, keeping keyword safety rules as a floor.

note: Clarify and act. When unsure, the copilot asks up to 2 clarifying questions with a menu built from the reservation's stage, instead of handing off. It can also resolve: cancel and refund, report an issue, resend entry, start a claim, message the host, email a receipt, with a confirm step for anything that moves money or speaks for the guest. Safety, disputes and requests for a person still hand off on the first message; every menu offers "I don't feel safe".
holdout_note: Holdout 2 reused: first-reply retrieval is unchanged from v2.1; only the conversation layer is new.
verdict: Resolved in conversation rises from 41% to 68% on holdout (every answerable contact) with zero wrong answers, using a simulated guest who picks the right option when it's shown, so treat it as a ceiling. First-message safety routing is still 75%; the menu's safety option catches the rest, but the release gate stays on the first message.
